purpose:
A decision is required by the
Shadow Authority on the structure of future Council Tax Support
Scheme for the new authorities.
content:
A decision is required by the
Shadow Authority on the structure of future Council Tax Support
Scheme for the new authorities.

RESOLVED

That    
(i)     the harmonisation of the Council
Tax Support schemes across West Surrey, from 1 April 2027 be agreed
in principle, subject to further consideration in September
2026;

           
(ii)    a bid to the
implementation programme board for funding from the implementation
programme fund be supported, noting that
the budget in respect of West Surrey
Council’s proportion of the modelling and
implementation costs will be £120,000;

           
(iii)    it be agreed that,
for modelling purposes, the central case as set out in the options
section, is used as the central benchmarking for scheme modelling
to compare the cost of different schemes;

           
(iv)   it be noted that the Senior
Responsible Officer of the Implementation Team, in consultation
with the relevant Portfolio Holder, shall undertake a procurement
exercise, in accordance with the West Surrey Shadow Authority
Contract and Procurement Procedure Rules, on behalf of both East
Surrey Shadow Authority and West Surrey Shadow Authority, for a
contractor, and authorise Surrey County Council to enter into the
relevant contracts for the work agreed under (ii) and (iii) above;
and

           
(v)    a report back be
received in September 2026 with the outcome of the modelling and further
recommendations for consideration of a harmonised
policy.
Reasons for recommendation:
Regulations provide that the Shadow Authority should make
reasonable efforts to prepare a council tax reduction scheme under
section 13A(2) of the Local Government Finance Act 1992 before 1
April 2027 [all other new unitary authorities have harmonised on
Vesting Day].  If this is not possible,
then they legally must be harmonised by 31 March 2029.
Local CTS reduces the council tax liability for low-income
households.  It is a highly visible
local welfare policy because it directly affects how much residents
are billed and what they can realistically afford to
pay.
CTS design influences whether residents face manageable bills or
are at risk of accruing greater arrears.  Even modest changes to awards, tapers, minimum
awards or income rules can matters significantly for households
already under financial pressure.
CTS rules shape billing, change in circumstances, discretionary
decisions, recovery activity and resident enquiries.  A clearer, more consistent scheme may support
simpler administration, although transition can still create
short-term complexity.
CTS sits at the intersection of fairness, affordability and
financial sustainability.  Decisions are
therefore likely to attract scrutiny from members, residents,
advice agencies and wider local partners.
topline: The West Surrey Shadow Authority has decided to harmonise the Council Tax Support schemes across the region, impacting low-income households and local authorities.

purpose:

content:
Direction required on whether
all existing policies to remain in place and to continue into the
new Unitary for each area / unless otherwise directed.
 

RESOLVED

That    
(i)     it be agreed in principle that discretionary council tax and
business rates policies should be harmonised across the
geographical area of West Surrey Council from
Vesting Day;

           
(ii)    the adoption of a
single harmonised Section 13A(1)(c) discretionary policy for West
Surrey Council be endorsed in
principle, applying a consistent framework for
hardship, exceptional circumstances, application requirements,
evidence, decision-making, review and appeals, subject to
further approval of such a policy;

           
(iii)    the adoption of a
single harmonised Section 47, discretionary business rates relief policy for West Surrey be
endorsed in principle, covering charitable
and not-for-profit relief, community and economic benefit, hardship
relief, local discounts, government-funded schemes administered
through Section 47 powers and subsidy control requirements,
subject to further approval of such a policy;

           
(iv)   further work be undertaken
to refine and complete the proposed policies, including consideration of the outcomes
of consultation, equality impact assessments and
implementation;

           
(v)    requests that
harmonised Council Tax and Business Rate discretionary relief
policies be brought back to the Shadow Executive on 16 December
2026 for recommendation to the Shadow Authority meeting on 14
January 2027 for formal adoption to be effective from Vesting Day;
and

           
(vi)   it be agreed that the
harmonised policies should be reviewed within twelve months of
implementation, and thereafter at least every three years, or
sooner where legislative, financial or operational changes require
review. 
Reasons for decision:
The recommendations are made to ensure that West Surrey Council
is able to operate from Vesting Day with clear, lawful and
consistent discretionary taxation policies.  Harmonising the policies will reduce the risk of
residents, businesses and voluntary organisations being treated
differently because of historic district or borough boundaries and
will provide a common basis for decision-making.
From an operational perspective, harmonisation is necessary to
support safe transition.  Revenues and
Benefits teams will need to administer billing, collection,
recovery, discounts, exemptions, reductions and reliefs from day
one.  Multiple inherited policies would
complicate system configuration, staff training, customer
communications, quality assurance and financial
monitoring.  A harmonised approach will
enable a single set of application forms, evidence standards,
decision templates, delegated authority levels, review arrangements
and management information reports for each new
authority.
A
harmonised approach is recommended under section 13a
of the Local Government Finance Act 1992 and Section
47 of the Local Government Finance Act 1988 and will allow
West Surrey Council to make fair, reasonable and evidence-based
decisions while retaining the ability to consider exceptional
circumstances.  A published and
consistent policy framework will support transparency, protect
against arbitrary or inconsistent decisions and assist officers in
applying discretion lawfully.
topline: The West Surrey Shadow Authority Executive has decided to harmonise discretionary council tax and business rates policies to ensure fair and consistent treatment across the geographical area.

content:
A decision is required to align
Council Tax discounts and premiums across the new authorities,
including arrangements for second homes, empty homes, uninhabitable
properties, care leavers, and SR1 (terminally ill)
cases.

RESOLVED

That    
(i)     a harmonised
approach be adopted to Council Tax Premiums across all constituent
authorities;

           
(ii)    a 100% premium be
applied on second homes, from the earliest lawful implementation
date, by giving notice in February 2027 to come into effect from 1
April 2028 in those areas where the premium does not currently
apply;

           
(iii)    long-term empty
property premiums be applied at the maximum levels permitted by
legislation for properties which are empty and
unfurnished:

a)     100% premium for
properties empty for one to five years;

b)     200% premium for
properties empty for five to ten years; and

c)     300%
premium for properties empty for more than ten years.

           
(iv)   all
mandatory statutory exemptions be maintained and the use of
discretionary reliefs be reviewed to ensure consistency across West
Surrey Council;

           
(v)    a formal consultation
be undertaken on the proposed harmonisation of Council Tax Premium
policies across West Surrey, with the outcomes of that consultation
to inform the development of a consistent policy for
residents;

           
(vi)   further work be undertaken
to refine and complete the proposed policy, including consideration
of the outcomes of consultation, financial modelling, equality
impact assessments and implementation; and

           
(vii)   a final harmonised Council
Tax Premiums policy be brought back to Full Council in December
2026 for consideration and approval, with a view to implementation
from Vesting Day.
Reasons for recommendation:
The Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023 introduced enhanced
powers for English local authorities to apply Council Tax Premiums
to long-term empty homes and, from April 2025, second
homes.  Councils may determine whether
to apply these premiums and at what level, subject to statutory
maximums.  Government guidance
emphasises that authorities should consider local housing pressures
and local circumstances when exercising these powers.
Across Surrey, housing affordability remains a significant
challenge, with strong demand for housing and limited supply in
many communities.  At the same time,
many dwellings remain either vacant for extended periods or are
used as second homes rather than as primary residences.
Consistency and Fairness - A harmonised approach would ensure
that residents across West Surrey are treated consistently,
reducing confusion and perceptions of inequity between neighbouring
areas that become part of the same local authority from vesting
day.  Differences in premium levels can
create administrative complexity and inconsistent outcomes for
property owners.
Supporting Housing Supply - Council Tax Premiums are intended to
encourage owners to bring properties back into occupation and to
make more effective use of existing housing stock. Government
guidance specifically identifies the use of premiums as a tool to
support local housing objectives and address housing
pressures.
Administrative Efficiency - A common framework would simplify
administration, communications, enforcement, and customer service
arrangements.  Shared policies would
also facilitate collaboration across West Surrey and support
consistent decision-making.
Financial Sustainability - Additional revenue generated through
premiums can contribute towards the cost of local services and
support housing-related initiatives. 
While revenue generation should not be the primary objective, a
harmonised approach would provide greater certainty in forecasting
and budgeting.
Proposed Harmonised Framework - The framework would operate
alongside all statutory exemptions and exceptions prescribed by
government regulations.  The exceptions
are prescribed by central government, where in certain instances
the premiums cannot be applied. 
Authorities would continue to exercise any discretionary powers in
accordance with agreed West Surrey policies.
Benefits - The proposed approach is expected to:

·            
Encourage occupation of underused housing
stock.

·            
Support housing availability for local
residents.

·            
Deliver greater consistency across West
Surrey.

·            
Reduce administrative complexity.

·            
Provide additional resources to support housing and
community priorities.

·            
Strengthen public understanding of Council Tax
Premium policies.
topline: The West Surrey Shadow Authority Executive has decided to harmonise Council Tax discounts and premiums, including applying a 100% premium on second homes and increasing premiums for long-term empty properties.

purpose:
To agree and endorse the
principles and approach to developing the West Surrey Corporate
Strategy and financial planning, in line with Best Value

content:
To agree and endorse the
principles and approach to developing the West Surrey Corporate
Strategy and financial planning, in line with Best Value
Standards.


RESOLVED

That    
(i)     the progress made
in building the evidence base and the undertaking of preparatory
work to support the development of the Corporate Strategy for the
West Surrey Council be noted;

           
(ii)    the emerging, early
draft vision, values and priorities be noted and endorsed as the
basis for further development of the Corporate Strategy;
and

           
(iii)    the recommended
option (Option 2) be
approved for further development of the Corporate
Strategy, including the proposed approach to resident, staff and
stakeholder engagement.

Reasons for decisions

The recommended approach supports the continued
development of a clear and robust Corporate Strategy for West
Surrey Council, providing visibility of progress and enabling
appropriate oversight and input as the emerging vision, values and
priorities are refined ahead of Vesting Day.  It also establishes a proportionate framework for
further development, ensuring that the Strategy remains
deliverable, aligned with local needs and organisational capacity,
and is consistent with Best Value principles and the Ministry of
Housing, Communities and Local Government’s
(“MHCLG’s”) Local Government Reorganisation
assurance requirements.

This approach is consistent with the expectation
that Elected Members play an active role in shaping the strategic
direction of the new Council.  It also
ensures compliance with the resolution of the West Surrey Shadow
Authority at its meeting on 21 May 2026, where it was resolved to
‘Refer all elements of the West Surrey Corporate Strategy,
including the timetable, planning, communication and drafting, to
the Executive Committee’ (covered under agenda item
12).

To consider service
configurations to be adopted for vesting day.

RESOLVED

That    
(i)     subject to a similar resolution
being made by the Executive of East Surrey Shadow Authority,
authority be provided in principle for the recommended
configuration of services to transition to East Surrey Council and
West Surrey Council, as set out in Appendix 1 of the report, to
enable the implementation team to progress with preparatory work,
whilst noting that such work is subject to the formal decision
making of the Shadow Authority when they further consider this
matter and make formal resolutions regarding service configuration
in September 2026;

           
(ii)    the principles being
used to recommend the proportionate split of activity for
disaggregated services between East Surrey Council and West Surrey
Council be approved as set out in the report, and it be noted that
recommendations on the basis of application of these will be
brought to the Shadow Executive for agreement in Autumn 2026;

           
(iii)    the proposed approach
to recommending which of East Surrey Council or West Surrey Council
will be the host authority for services where no clear
location-based rationale exists be agreed as set out in the
report;

           
(iv)   authority be delegated to
the Head of Paid Service in consultation with the Leader of West
Surrey Shadow Authority, relevant Portfolio Holders and the Senior
Responsible Officer (“SRO”) to revisit and amend any
recommended service configurations should this become necessary in
light of central government direction and/or delivery
requirements;

           
(v)    it be noted that
material budget pressures and potential savings arising from the
recommended service configurations will be identified and included
for consideration within the wider strategic and financial planning
process; and

           
(vi)   it be noted that East Surrey
Shadow Executive is considering the report at their equivalent
meeting on 20 July 2026, and that decisions taken by each authority
will necessitate ongoing joint working across the Executives
throughout the transition period to support a successful
implementation.
Reasons for decision
The approach and principles which shape recommendations for how
services transition are set out in the programme’s
Implementation Plan, and the recommendations have been developed in
line with these, with the guiding principle for the programme of
‘transition not transformation’.  The focus of the recommendations is therefore to
establish arrangements which support service continuity and are
deliverable at Vesting Day, rather than undertake wider service
redesign at this stage.

(ii)    consent be provided to

route optimisation in line with the provisions set out in the
appendices to this report;

           
(iii)    consent be provided
to Runnymede Borough Council to dispose of an asset in Egham
(1);

           
(iv)   consent be provided to
Runnymede Borough Council to dispose of an asset in Egham
(2);

           
(v)    consent be provided to
Runnymede Borough Council to dispose of Land;

           
(vi)   consent be provided to
Runnymede Borough Council to enter into an agreement for a new
letting in Egham (1);

           
(vii)   consent be provided to
Runnymede Borough Council to enter into an agreement for a new
letting in Egham (2);

           
(viii)  consent be provided to Runnymede
Borough Council to enter into an agreement for Lease Renewal in
Egham;

           
(ix)   the Chief Finance Officer be
authorised to amend the General Consent, to include a new general consent to allow leases, easements and
wayleaves,that would otherwise require consent of the Shadow
Executive, to be approved by the predecessor
councils; and

           
(x)    Authorise the Chief
Finance Officer, to amendthe General Consent number 9,to cap community grants to be a maximum of the average
of the last 5 years
Reasons for recommendation:
Councils have a statutory duty to arrange for the collection of
household waste and keep land and highways clear of litter under
the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and this new contract will
ensure continuity of these key statutory services for residents and
administrative areas from 6 June 2027.
The collection review optimisation at Runnymede Borough Council
will ensure continued delivery of reliable, safe and efficient
collection services for residents.
The recommended disposals at Runnymede Borough Council ensure
that the Council is holding the most appropriate assets moving into
vesting day.  They also allow a review
of the debt portfolio giving the opportunity to repay
debt.
The letting and lease renewals at Runnymede Borough Council will
ensure that rental income is maximised and units are
occupied.

content:
This report seeks approval from the Leader of the Council,
acting in the capacity as Shareholder of ThamesWey Limited (TWL),
for the creation of two new subsidiary companies within the
ThamesWey group as part of the proposed corporate restructuring of
ThamesWey Housing Limited (THL). The restructuring is required to
facilitate the sale of THL and its residential portfolio, in line
with the Council’s strategic objective to divest from its
commercial interests and reduce its overall debt
position.
The two new companies proposed are:
1.  ThamesWey Commercial Ltd, to hold
commercial assets currently within the group; and
2.  TH Management Ltd, to separate
THL operational and staffing functions from the current group
personnel company TSCL.


RECOMMENDATIONS
The Leader of the
Council, acting in the capacity as Shareholder of TWL,
Resolved that

1.          
the creation of two new subsidiary companies, ThamesWey Commercial
Ltd and TH Management Ltd, as part of the ThamesWey corporate
restructuring be approved;

2.          
the proposed restructuring of HL and its group structure to
facilitate the disposal of the housing portfolio be approved;
and

3.          
the Chief Executive be authorised to take all necessary actions to
implement the restructuring, including the incorporation of the new
entities and approval of agreements required to give effect to the
restructuring, including agreements relating to the transfer of
assets and the release and/or transfer of security.
Decision
Details
Decision sought:
Approval to create two new subsidiary companies within the
ThamesWey structure and approve the associated restructuring of
THL.
Companies to be
created: ThamesWey Commercial Ltd and TH Management Ltd.
Purpose of
ThamesWey Commercial Ltd: To hold commercial assets currently
within the group.
Purpose of TH
Management Ltd: To separate THL operational and staffing functions
from the rest of the TWL.
Decision-maker:
The Leader of the Council, acting in the capacity as Shareholder,
as the decision relates to changes to the corporate structure of a
wholly owned company and the incorporation of new subsidiary
entities.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to approve the creation of two new subsidiary companies within the ThamesWey group for the restructuring of ThamesWey Housing Limited.

purpose:

content:
Decision on the outcome of the waste
collection re-tender.


The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the
bidder who submitted the most advantageous tender (Preferred
Bidder) be awarded the joint contract to deliver waste collection
services in Woking (Joint Contract) commencing from 6 June 2027 up
to and including 5 June 2034, with the option, but not the
obligation, for the participating authorities and the service
provider to agree to extend the Joint Contract by one or more
successive consecutive periods until 2048 and in doing so, the
following is agreed;

a.   
The Council enters into the Joint Contract with each
of the partner authorities and the Preferred Bidder (such contract
inter alia providing that the partner authorities will have joint
and several liability to the contractor and against which they
indemnify each other against their breach);

b.   
The Council enters into the Inter-Authority
Agreement (IAA) with each of the other partner authorities,
Elmbridge Borough Council, Mole Valley District Council and Surrey
Heath Borough Council, which will regulate the relationship between
the partner authorities (as necessitated by entry into the Joint
Contract), continues the role of the shared contract management
office (CMO) (hosted by Surrey Heath Borough Council as the
administering authority) and the required governance arrangements,
including the terms of reference for the Joint Waste Collection
Services Committee;

c.   
Pursuant to section 9EA of the Local Government Act
2000, Regulations 9 and 11 of the Local Authorities (Arrangements
for the Discharge of Functions)(England) 2012 and all other
enabling powers of the functions of the Council under section 45 of
the Environmental Protection Act 1990, the Council makes
arrangements for the joint discharge of such of those functions as
are set out in the IAA by the Joint Waste Collection Services
Committee established for that purpose;

d.   
That the provisions of the CMO provided in the IAA
is entered into as a contract for services in order to deliver
co-operation between public bodies as envisaged by Schedule 2 of
the Procurement Act 2023;

e.   
The Council grants a lease of part of Monument Road,
Woking depot to the Preferred Bidder commencing on 6 June 2027 and
co-terminous with the Council’s
participation in the Joint Contract;

f.    
To approve the drawdown of £4.2m of funds from
the provisional capital programme to the approved capital programme
for the purpose of funding the purchase of the replacement fleet in
accordance with the Council’s obligations under the Joint
Contract; and

g.   
Delegate to the Strategic Director of Place and
Digital to make all decisions and take all actions in respect of
any agreements or other instruments as are reasonably necessary to
give effect to (or are ancillary to) the above on behalf of the
Council.

Reason: To secure a compliant, value
for money contract that ensures continuity of a statutory service
beyond June 2027 and enables timely mobilisation, and to establish
the legal and governance framework required to deliver and manage
the Joint Contract effectively across the partner
authorities.
topline: The Executive has decided to award a joint waste collection services contract to a preferred bidder for up to 2048, ensuring continuity of service and establishing a legal framework for effective management.

purpose: Decision on a proposal for energy support.
content:
Decision on a proposal for energy support.


The Executive Resolved

That  (i)   
financial support be approved in principle to The
Lightbox of up to £131,000 over a maximum two-year period,
subject to the following conditions being
satisfied;

(a) 
that a request for financial support
has been submitted to the Council;

(b) 
that adequate independently verified evidence has
been provided to the Council demonstrating that the increase in
tariffs would result in The Lightbox being unable to continue its
operations;

(c) 
the Council being satisfied,
following receipt of a request for financial support and receipt of
satisfactory legal, financial and subsidy control advice as
appropriate, that;

(i)    
either the provision of the requested
financial support will not provide a subsidy; or

(ii)   
the provision of the requested financial support can
be given using either the exemption for minimum financial
assistance or the exemption for SPEI (services of public economic
interest) assistance in section 36 and 28 of the Subsidy Control
Act, 2022; and

         
(ii)   authority be delegated
to the Council’s Chief Executive in
consultation with the Strategic Director – Finance and
Economy and the Strategic Director – Governance and Corporate
to determine the outcome of any requests for financial support in
line with the provisions in Recommendation (i), following receipt of satisfactory legal,
financial and subsidy control advice.

Reason: The decision is required to
enable the Council to respond in a targeted and proportionate way
to the impact of the TEL tariff change on an organisation that
occupies a Council-owned asset.  The
decision is also required to seek in principle approval of the
financial support, subject to various conditions being
satisfied.  The proposed support is
considered to represent a prudent course of action which accords
with the Council’s fiduciary duties because it helps mitigate
the risk of higher costs and liabilities falling on the Council
that could arise if The Lightbox became financially unviable, while
allowing time for transition and adjustment.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve financial support for The Lightbox to prevent it from becoming financially unviable.

Limited shares in ThamesWey Housing Limited; and

       
(iii)  the recommendations from the
Resource and Finance Scrutiny Committee held on 9 June 2026 be
accepted.

objective as set out in the ThamesWey business plan approved by the
Shareholder Executive Committee in September 2025.  It is also a key component of the Council’s
Company Divestment Strategy and debt reduction plan, which forms an
essential part of the Council’s Improvement and Recovery
Plan.

purpose:

content:
The Executive Resolved

That (i)   it be noted there has been a change of
approach to the marketing (and disposal) of the VSWL and WBC assets
which is set out in the report from that approved in the Executive
report dated 18th March 2026;

       
(ii)  approval be
grantedfor the marketing and disposal of
Wolsey Walk, ThamesWey Residential
Holdings and Export House as freehold disposals, distinct from the
disposal of the VSWL assets;

       
(iii)  the Portfolio Holder –
Finance and Economy be authorised to approve the preferred
bidder(s), for Wolsey Walk, Export House and ThamesWey Residential Holdings, based on a
recommendation from the Council’s Chief Executive and
following receipt of advice on the legal and financial implications
from the Council’s Statutory Officers;

        (iv) approval
be granted for the Council to enter into long lease(s) arrangements
for the Red and Green car parks granted by VSWL at a peppercorn
rent subject to Heads of Terms to be authorised by the Portfolio
Holder based on officer advice;

       
(v)  approval be granted for the Council
to enter into any ancillary agreements/arrangements relating to the
Red and Green car parks with VSWL and other parties as may be
required to facilitate the disposal of VSWL assets;

        (vi) approval
be granted for the Council to enter into agreements/arrangements
which are ancillary to the disposal of VSWL assets which may
include the granting of easements/cross rights and transfers of
minor pockets of land;

        (vii)
authority be delegated to the Chief Executive to take all necessary
steps to effect the decisions in recommendations (ii) – (vi)
, including but not limited to determining the appropriate time and
mechanism for commencement of the marketing of the assets,
negotiating the terms of any required documents/agreements and
entering into agreements as may be required to effect the decisions
in recommendations (ii) – (vi); and

     
(viii)  the
recommendations from the Resource and Finance Scrutiny Committee
held on 9 June 2026 be accepted.

Reason:  A
decision is required
to grant approval to take an alternative approach to the marketing
of VSWL assets, based on advice received from joint agents (Knight
Frank and TT&G) appointed by VSWL.

             
A decision is required to enter into a long leasehold arrangement
with VSWL for the Red and Green car parks and other ancillary
agreements and arrangements relating to the car parks.
The Council is seeking a long leasehold of the Red
and Green car parks to be put in place with VSWL so that, in the
event that the sale of VSWL freeholds is approved, the
Council’s revenue stream from the car parks will be
maintained and protected.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the marketing and disposal of certain assets, as well as entering into long lease arrangements for Red and Green car parks.

Keynes Ltd on behalf of the Council;

       
(iii)  authority be delegated to the
Portfolio Holder for Finance and Economy to agree the final terms
of sale of ThamesWey Central Milton
Keynes Ltd, following receipt of final details of the sale proposal
from the Board of ThamesWey Central
Milton Keynes Ltd, advice from the Council’s Statutory
Officers and appropriate external legal, financial and other advice
as may be required; and

        (iv) following
completion of the sale, TCMK be authorised to enter into all
documents as reasonably required by TCMK to facilitate the
disposal.

The Executive Recommended to Council

That (v)  the debt for
equity swap to facilitate the disposal of ThamesWey Central Milton Keynes Limited (the
details of which are set out in Appendix 2 to the report) be
approved.

Reason:  The disposal of TCMK is a key strategic objective as set out in the
ThamesWey business plan approved by the
Shareholder Executive Committee.  It is
also a key component of the Council’s Company Divestment
Strategy and debt reduction plan, which forms an essential part of
the Council’s Improvement and Recovery
Plan.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the disposal of ThamesWey Central Milton Keynes Ltd, subject to a debt for equity swap, as part of the Council's Company Divestment Strategy and debt reduction plan.

purpose:
To outline and seek approval for the approach
to divestment in companies and marketing their disposal.
content:
To outline and seek approval for the approach
to divestment in companies and marketing their disposal.


The Executive Resolved

That (i)   the commencement of marketing by Victoria
Square Woking Limited of the Marches residential units, Hilton
Hotel and retail assets be approved;

       
(ii)  the draft marketing plans (which
may be subject to further future change) included at Appendix 1 of
the report for the disposal of the Marches, Hilton Hotel and retail
premises be carefully considered and comments be provided for
consideration by the Board of Victoria Square Woking
Limited;

       
(iii)  the Board of Victoria Square
Woking Limited be required to provide monthly updates on the
implementation and any changes to the marketing plans to the
Shareholder Executive Committee at its meetings;

        (iv) the
Leader of the Council on behalf of the Shareholder and as advised
by officers following receipt of satisfactory legal, financial and
marketing advice be authorised to take such decisions as may be
required of the Shareholder (including approval of the
nature/structure of the disposal of the assets) to facilitate the
implementation of the Victoria Square Woking Limited marketing
plans;

       
(v)  it be noted that the Board of
Victoria Square Woking Limited will seek approval from the
Executive on the preferred bidder and final sale terms;

        (vi) the
outline proposals set out in the report for determining an
appropriate way forward by ThamesWey Energy Limited which will
require a decision from the Executive at a later date be noted;
and

        (vii) the
position on car parking arrangements which serve the Victoria
Square assets be noted.

Reason:  The disposal of
the assets is in line with the VSWL business plan approved by the
Council’s Shareholder Executive Committee.  The proposal is also in line with the
Council’s Company Divestment Strategy which is a key plank of
the Commercial Workstream within the Council’s Improvement
and Recovery Plan.

Cllr Barker, Leader of the Council.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the marketing and disposal of residential units, a hotel, and retail assets by Victoria Square Woking Limited.

purpose: To agree an asset sale.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That (i)   disposal of the freehold interest of Wolsey
Walk be approved;

       
(ii)  it be agreed a combined portfolio
of predominantly retail/leisure/office assets currently owned by
Woking Borough Council (WBC), Victoria Square Woking Ltd (VSWL) and
ThamesWey (TW) should be combined to
form a single investment package for sale;

       
(iii)  following a competitive open
market disposal process, the combined sites comprising Wolsey
Walk/Victoria Square/Export House and ThamesWey holdings should be sold to a recommended
purchaser;

        (iv) authority
be delegated to the Strategic Director – Finance and
Resources, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder, to market the
portfolio in discussion with all relevant stakeholders including
VSWL and TW;

       
(v)  on completion of the proposed
marketing exercise to submit details of the proposed preferred
bidder(s) to the Executive for approval;

        (vi) the
commercially sensitive information in support of the recommendation
to dispose set out in the Part II report, be noted; and

        (vii) it be
noted that work will be undertaken by officers to enhance the
security of loans granted by the Council to council owned companies
which will be the subject of a future report to Full
Council.

Reason:  The Improvement and Recovery Programme published in August 2023
recognised that the Council was in a challenging financial position
and one of the core aims of the Recovery Programme was to
rationalise the property portfolio to reduce the significant debt
attributable to property assets.  In
January 2024 an Asset Management Plan was prepared demonstrating an
orderly disposal of key WBC assets over a three-year timeline from
2024-2027 which was subsequently presented to Government in August
2024. The approved Asset Management Plan provides for the disposal
of the Wolsey Walk Retail investment and ancillary holdings during
the period quarter one to quarter four 2026.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the disposal of Wolsey Walk and combine a portfolio of assets for sale to address the Council's financial challenges.

purpose:
To recommend to Council the updated Housing
Standards Enforcement Policy, and Housing Standards CPN Policy for
adoption.
content:
To recommend to Council the updated Housing
Standards Enforcement Policy, and Housing Standards CPN Policy for
adoption.


The Executive Recommended to Council

That (i)   
the Housing Standards
Enforcement Policy and the Housing Standards Civil Penalty Notice
Policy be adopted and come into force on 01 May
2026;

         
(ii)   the additional clauses be added relating to parts of
the Renters’ Rights Act that will be implemented at a later
date with the authority of the Strategic Director – Place and
Digital;

         
(iii)  the Delegated Authority for the new legislation and
all offences in the policy are entered into the Constitution and
assigned to the Strategic Director – Place and Digital;
and

         
(iv) Minor adjustments to
both policies are delegated to the Strategic Director – Place
and Digital.

Reason: The adoption of these two new
policies in place of the Council’s current policies is
required to enable the Council to undertake its new duties under
the Renters’ Rights Act 2025.
topline: The Executive has decided to recommend the adoption of updated Housing Standards Enforcement Policy and Housing Standards CPN Policy.

purpose:
To recommend to Council the approval of
various housing operational policies covering compliance,
maintenance and management of our housing stock.
content:
The Executive Recommended to Council

That (i)    the
Damp and Mould Policy be approved; and

         
(ii)   the Strategic Director
– People and Communities, in consultation with the Portfolio
Holder for Housing, be authorised to make minor amendments to the
Policy as required.

Reason: To ensure that the Council
has up to date and transparent policies in place that meet the
requirements of the Regulator of Social Housing and Consumer
Standards.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the Damp and Mould Policy to ensure up to date and transparent policies for residents in social housing.

purpose:
To agree an extension to the Housing Repairs
and Maintenance contract.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the final 2-year contract extension
for the Housing Responsive Repairs Contract with Mountjoy Limited
be agreed for the period 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2029;
and

         
(ii)   authority be delegated to
the Strategic Director – People and Communities, in
consultation with the Portfolio Holder, to take all necessary steps
to affect the decision.

Reason: To ensure the Council can meet its statutory
and regulatory obligations in respect to Housing
Repairs.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve a 2-year contract extension for the Housing Responsive Repairs Contract with Mountjoy Limited.

purpose:
To agree the Woking For All Strategy
refresh.
content:
The Executive Recommended to Council

That (i)    the
refreshed Woking for All Strategy be approved; and

         
(ii)   progress against the actions
be noted.

Reason: To ensure that the refreshed Woking for All
Strategy reflects the Council’s current position and the
significant changes occurring in local government, and to confirm
robust performance monitoring of the Council’s priorities and
objectives.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the refreshed Woking for All Strategy and note progress against the actions.

purpose:
To provide an update on the Lakeview Estate
and Housing Fire Safety Remedial Works procurement processes.
content:
To provide an update on the Lakeview Estate
and Housing Fire Safety Remedial Works procurement processes.


The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the procurement status and programme
update for the Lakeview Estate Refurbishment Scheme be
noted;

         
(ii)   new contracts be awarded to
Amber Construction Services (Amber) and Mulalley and Company
Limited (Mulalley) to continue to deliver the ongoing fire safety
remediation works programme through a Direct Award using the South
East Consortium (SEC) Framework; and

         
(iii)  the Head of Housing Assets, in
consultation with the Strategic Director – People and
Communities and Portfolio Holder for Housing, be authorised to
finalise and implement the above appointments and extensions,
subject to Legal and Finance sign?off.

Reason: To avoid disruption and delay to the
Council’s fire safety remediation programme and maintain the
Council’s ability to discharge its statutory landlord
responsibilities.
topline: The Executive has decided to award new contracts for fire safety remediation works on the Lakeview Estate

purpose:
To provide quarterly reports on the progress
of projects in the interests of financial prudence and corporate
governance.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the report be received; and

         
(ii)   the project monitoring at
Appendix 1 to the report be noted.

Reason: To apply performance management to Council
projects.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve recommendations for project monitoring of Council projects.

purpose:
To award the contract for Security Guarding
Services.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the contract for Security Guarding
Services be awarded for an initial contract period of two years,
with two optional one-year extensions; and

         
(ii)   authority be delegated to
the Strategic Director – Finance and Resources and Strategic
Director – Governance, Corporate Services and Monitoring
Officer, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder, to take all
necessary steps to affect the decision to enter into a relevant
contract, including finalising the call-off terms under CCS RM6257
in the form approved by Legal Services, raising the necessary
Purchase Order(s), and executing the contract under
seal.

Reason: To allow the Council to award a new contract
to Bidvest Noonan effective from the 1 April 2026 and to ensure the
continued delivery of Security Guarding Services at key Council
operated properties.
topline: The Executive has decided to award a contract for Security Guarding Services for a period of two years with optional extensions.

purpose:
To award the contract for Security Systems and
Associated Critical Infrastructure.
content:
To award the contract for Security Systems and
Associated Critical Infrastructure.


The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the contract for Security Systems and
Associated Critical Infrastructure be awarded for an initial
contract period of two years, with two optional one-year
extensions; and

         
(ii)   authority be delegated to
the Strategic Director – Finance and Resources and Strategic
Director – Governance, Corporate Services and Monitoring
Officer, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder, to take all
necessary steps to affect the decision to  enter into a relevant contract, including
finalising the call-off terms under CCS RM6257 in the form approved
by Legal Services, raising the necessary Purchase Order(s), and
executing the contract under seal.

Reason: To allow the Council to award a contract to
OCS Group UK Limited, effective from 1 April 2026 and to ensure the
continued delivery of essential maintenance to security systems and
infrastructure throughout the Borough.
topline: The Executive has decided to award a contract for Security Systems and Associated Critical Infrastructure.

purpose:
To receive details of RIPA authorisations
during 2025 calendar year.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the proposed changes to the Regulation
of Investigatory Powers Act policy included at Appendix 1 to the
report be noted; and

         
(ii)   the update on the use of
Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 during the 2025
calendar year be noted.

Reason: To ensure that the Council is kept up to
date and can monitor the Council’s use of covert surveillance
and investigatory powers and ensure that the policy is up to
date.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve recommendations for changes to the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act policy and update on its use during the 2025 calendar year.

purpose:
To agree consultation and main principles of
PSPO.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    public consultation on the draft
Proposed Woking Town Centre Public Spaces Protection Order should
be undertaken;

         
(ii)   authority is delegated to
the Strategic Director – Communities and Housing to take all
necessary steps to effect the decision in (i) including all
necessary publications and notifications as required by the
legislation; and

         
(iii)  it be noted that a further report
will be provided to the Executive setting out the results of the
consultation and proposing next steps.

Reason: To seek approval to proceed with a
consultation on a mechanism to tackle and reduce
anti-social-behaviour in Woking.
topline: The Executive has decided to conduct a public consultation on a draft Proposed Woking Town Centre Public Spaces Protection Order to address anti-social behaviour.

purpose:
To write off debts over
£10,000.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That the debts listed in Appendix 1 to the report be
written off.

Reason: When debts have become demonstrably
irrecoverable, writing them off represents good financial
management. It allows staff to concentrate on recoverable debts and
ensures that the level of recoverable debtors within the
Council’s accounts is accurate and represents a true and fair
reflection of the Council’s financial position.
topline: The Executive has decided to write off unrecoverable debts for good financial management.

purpose:
To agree next steps and timetable to bring
forward the new Local Plan for Woking.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    the proposed timetable for the new
local plan is agreed; and

         
(ii)   delegated authority is
granted to the Head of Planning, in consultation with the Portfolio
Holder for Planning, to make any necessary amendments and to
publish the timetable and “notice of intention to commence
local plan preparation” no later than 30 June
2026.

Reason: To make sure the 30-month timeline can be
achieved, it is necessary for Members to agree the proposed
timetable and to grant delegated authority to make minor amendments
if needed to avoid any delays.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the proposed timetable for a new local plan.

purpose:
To recommend to Council a Generative
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy.
content:
The Executive Resolved

That (i)   further in-person training for users on the
use of Copilot and other AI tools be noted;

       
(ii)   Officers to explore and
clarify the availability of full Microsoft 365 and Copilot access
for Councillors;

       
(iii)  alternatives to the single vendor
model, with only Copilot as a permitted tool, be kept under review;
and

The Executive Recommended to Council

That the Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Policy, attached as Appendix 1 to the report, be adopted, subject
to the amendments agreed by the Executive.

Reason:  To ensure that Council employees, Members and third parties using
generative AI tools when carrying out Council business do so in a
lawful, secure, and ethical manner which is aligned to Council
values, information governance requirements, and statutory
duties.
topline: The Executive has decided to adopt a Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy for the use of AI tools in Council business.

purpose:
Financial regulation 12.14 states:

Any debt due to the Council may only be written off with the
authorisation of the Executive - except insofar as an individual
debt does not exceed £10,000.00; the initial authority may be
given by the Chief Finance Officer, who shall be required to
publish periodically reports of the debts that have been written
off, in accordance with the delegated authority.

The Business Support Manager is exercising an authority delegated
to them by the CFO for debts up to £5,000.00.

The Financial Services Manager is exercising an authority delegated
to them by the CFO for debts up to £10,000.00.

The Financial Director (Chief Finance Officer) is exercising this
delegated authority/recommendation for debts over
£10,000.00.

There is delegated authority for Business Support Officers to
authorise small debt write offs of £100.00 and
under.
topline: The Chief Finance Officer has decided to approve financial recommendations.

content:
The Council had before it a report on the recommendations from
the Executive and the Audit and Governance Committee, setting out
the extracts from the minutes of the meetings held on 5 February
and 26 February 2026.  In accordance
with the Constitution, the recommendations were deemed to have been
moved and seconded.
The Mayor explained that the budget items under agenda items 9A
to 9E would be determined together with agenda item 10, General
Fund Budget and Council Tax Setting before the Council would move
to the recommendations of the Audit and Governance
Committee.
The Portfolio Holder would introduce the budget items as a
whole, following which the Councillors would be invited to debate
the proposals.  The Portfolio Holder
would address any points raised at the end of the debate, before
the Councillors were invited to determine the recommendations in
the reports.
topline: The Council has decided to approve budget recommendations following debates on various agenda items.

content:
Resolved

That (i)     Council acknowledges the Section
151 Officer’s s25 report on the robustness of the proposed
budget and the adequacy of the Council’s reserves, as set out
in Appendix 3 to the report, including the factors which underpin
the budget and specifically the need for exceptional financial
support to balance the budget;

       
(ii)    it be noted that the
financial position has been based on the final Local Government
Finance Settlement announced on 9 February 2026;

       
(iii)    it be noted that the
net cost of services position includes savings and pressures
recommended for approval by Executive on 5 February
2026;

       
(iv)   it be noted that Exceptional
Financial Support (EFS) is required to balance the 2026/27 budget
and that this has been granted by MHCLG, as per Appendices 1 and 6
to the report;

       
(v)    the Council’s
reserves position be noted;

       
(vi)   it be noted that work on the
medium-term financial position will continue during 2026/27 through
the Local Government Reorganisation process;

       
(vii)   the full net cost of
services requirement for 2026/27, including the impact of the
historic borrowing position is £150.2m, be agreed;

       
(viii)  the Council increases its share
of Council Tax for a Band D household by £8.94 (3.00%), with
other bands increased in line with the formula, be
agreed;

       
(ix)   an amount of Council Tax be
set for each valuation band in accordance with Section 30 of the
Local Governance Finance Act, 1992 as set out in the Council Tax
Resolution in Appendix 4 to the report, be agreed;

       
(x)    the existing Council
Tax Support Scheme be retained for 2026/27, but updated to reflect
indexation and statutory changes; and

       
(xi)   quarterly updates on
progress against the delivery of the Improvement and Recovery Plan,
and budget monitoring for the revenue and capital positions,
continue to be required.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for the 2026/27 budget, including a 3.00% increase in Council Tax for a Band D household.

That (i)    subject to Ministry of Housing,
Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)’s confirmation of

approved.

purpose:

Budgets for 2026-27.
content:
The Executive Recommended to Full Council on 2 March
2026

That (i)    the
£2.7m of new savings in 2026/27 as set-out in Appendix 1 to
the report be agreed, subject to any comments received from
Resource and Finance Scrutiny Committee;

         
(ii)   the £3.3m of new
growth pressures in 2026/27 as set-out in Appendix 2 to the report
be agreed, subject to any comments received from Resource and
Finance Scrutiny Committee;

         
(iii)  the position of the Business
Rates and Council Tax Collection Fund, including the brought
forward surplus/deficit position and the Council Tax and Business
Rates bases for 2026/27 as set out in Section 10 of the report be
noted and agreed;

         
(iv) the Management of Change and Flexible Use of Capital Receipts
budgets proposed at Appendices 4 and 5 to the report be approved;
and

         
(v)  it be noted that Full Council on 2
March 2026 will receive a final report from the Strategic Director
– Finance and Resources to seek final, formal approval of the
Council's budget, the Exceptional Financial Support and Council Tax
for 2026/27.

Reason: The contents of the report is to ensure open
and transparent governance in the financial affairs of the Council
in balancing the 2026/27 Budget, and the Medium Term Financial
Strategy (MTFS).
topline: The Executive has decided to approve new savings, growth pressures, and budget allocations for the 2026/27 fiscal year.

The Executive Resolved

extension be approved of the existing contractual arrangements
between the Council and Tile Hill Interim and Executive Limited

the provision of specialist support to the Council for the
continued delivery of the Company Divestment Strategy and Asset
Rationalisation Programme, taking into account the information in
the Appendix 1 (in Part 2); and

delivery of the Company Divestment Strategy and its own Asset
Rationalisation Programme, upon which the Government’s debt
relief for Woking is dependent.
topline: The Executive has decided to extend contractual arrangements with Tile Hill Interim and Executive Limited to support the Council's divestment strategy and asset rationalisation program.

purpose:

infrastructure within Woking.

content:
The Council received a report which proposed the re-designation
of three neighbourhood forums for the areas of Hook Heath, Hoe
Valley and Pyford.  It was noted that
whilst the designation of a neighbourhood area was made in
perpetuity, neighbourhood forum designations lasted for five
years.  The three forums had submitted
the information necessary for redesignation and a consultation had
been undertaken to seek local views.
The consultation responses had been overwhelmingly in favour of
supporting the re-designation of the three forums and accordingly
the Council was recommended to confirm the re-designations for a
further five years.
The Portfolio Holder for planning, Councillor Morales,
introduced the proposals and reported on the outcomes of the
consultation, noting that the majority of respondents in each of
the three areas had expressed support for the neighbourhood
forums.  The number of responses
received were sufficient to redesignate the three forums, ensuring
that the areas would be able to benefit from the opportunities to
establish a neighbourhood plan and access Community Infrastructure
Levy funds.  The forums would be able to
engage with the local communities to identify those issues
important to residents such as footpaths, seating and
lighting.

Resolved

That  (i)    the re-designation of Hook Heath
Neighbourhood Forum be agreed;

         
(ii)   the re-designation of Hoe
Valley Neighbourhood Forum be agreed; and

         
(iii)  the re-designation of Pyrford
Neighbourhood Forum be agreed.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the re-designation of neighbourhood forums in Hook Heath, Hoe Valley, and Pyrford.

content:
To receive a report on Investment Debt
Repayment and Standstill 2025-26 and 2026-27.

It
was noted that the Executive had further received a Part 2 report
in respect of the investment, debt repayment and standstill
position which had included commercially sensitive information and
was now referred to under Agenda Item 15.  The Mayor advised that the Council would consider
Items 9e and 15a together and that the topic would be discussed in
public until a point was reached at which one or more members asked
to discuss information which was restricted.  The recommendations of both Item 9e and Item 15a
would be taken together at the end of the discussions.
Councillor Roberts, Portfolio Holder for Finance, introduced the
recommendations of the Executive, advising
that the report set out the proposed approach to the Council's
lending arrangements with Victoria Square Woking Limited for the
year ahead.  Since the intervention in
2023 and the Section 114 notice, the Council had been implementing
the improvement and recovery plan, a key part of which was the
orderly and responsible exit from commercial activity.
It
was noted that a debt standstill for 2025 -2026 had been agreed by
the Council to keep Victoria Square Woking Limited solvent whilst
proper controls were established and preparations for disposal were
made.  The company was now operating
transparently with regular independent monitoring of solvency and
with a much clearer understanding of its true financial position.
As a result, an orderly and solvent disposal of Victoria Square
assets was deliverable. 
A
level of stability would be needed during the marketing of the
assets and accordingly a further debt standstill was
proposed.  The recommended approach
would protect value, avoid unnecessary losses and keep the Council
on the recovery path. 
Finally, it was noted that the Council had received a cash sweep
of approximately £340,000, the first surplus since the S114
had been announced.
The Mayor asked the Councillors to indicate whether they wished
to discuss any element of the restricted information originally
provided to the Executive.  Members
confirmed that this would not be necessary and accordingly the
Mayor directed the Council to the recommendations before them under
both Agenda Item 9E and 15A.

Resolved

That  (i)    it be noted that the Council will be
requesting Exceptional Financial Support for 2026/27 and this
request will incorporate the interest and minimum revenue provision
costs in relation to the loans made to the company and the debt
standstill and debt sweep contained within the report;

         
(ii)   a 2026/27 financial year
investment debt repayment standstill on the Council’s
investment loans to Victoria Square Woking Limited be approved
(subject to the conditions and caveats set out in the report and
subject to confirmation of Exceptional Financial Support from
central government) for the financial year 2026/27 as set out in
recommendation (i); and

         
(iii)  the findings in the Part II
report set out under Agenda Item 15 of the Executive agenda titled
Investment Debt Repayment and Standstill 2025-26 and 2026-27 be
noted.
topline: The Council has decided to approve a debt standstill and repayment plan for Victoria Square Woking Limited to ensure solvency and responsible exit from commercial activity.

purpose:

content:
To consider an updated Complaints Policy,
which meets the requirements of the relevant Ombudsman and brings
corporate and housing complaints together under one policy.

The Leader of the Council, Councillor Barker, introduced the
recommendation of the Executive which proposed the adoption of a
revised Complaints Policy for the Authority.  The new policy sought to streamline and improve
complaints handling processes at the Council in line with national
standards set by the Local Government and
Social Care Ombudsman, bringing together housing, tenant and other
complaints into a single system. 
The new approach sought to be clearer and more accessible for
residents and set a shorter timeframe for the Council to
respond.  The measures would also enable
improvements to the reporting of complaints to enable the Council
to scrutinise any trends.
It
was noted that the proposals had been reviewed by the Finance and
Resources Committee at its meeting on 4 November, the outcomes of
which had been reported to the Executive.  The Executive had proposed a number of changes to
the draft policy as a result and a revised copy had been circulated
with the agenda for Council.
The Leader advised that the Council Officers had worked to
ensure that there were sufficient resources to ensure that the
Council would be able to meet the new response deadline of ten
days.  The new policy, to be fully
implemented from April 2026, would include complaints raised
against some of the Council’s service providers and would
align with the approaches of the neighbouring Authorities which
would form the West Surrey Unitary Authority in the coming
years.
Members welcomed the proposals and thanked Officers for their
support and responses to the suggestions of the Scrutiny
Committee.

Resolved

That the draft Woking Borough Council (WBC)
Complaints Policy included at Appendix 1 to the report be approved,
subject to the amendments agreed by the Executive.
topline: The Council has decided to approve an updated Complaints Policy to streamline and improve complaints handling processes.

content:
The Council had before it the minutes of the meeting
of Council held on 25 September 2025. 
The Leader of the Council considered that the minutes did not fully
cover the scope of the discussion about a motion on Gaza, which had
been submitted by Councillor Akberali and had been deemed by the
Council's Chief Executive to be invalid.  The motion had therefore not been debated at the
meeting.  

The Leader moved that the minutes should be amended
to:

·               
reflect the fact that a motion had been submitted by
Councillor Akberali which had been deemed by the Chief Executive to
be invalid and therefore not included in the agenda; and

·               
reflect the fact that a discussion did take place at
the meeting between the Chief Executive, Mayor and Councillor
Akberali about the motion which had been deemed to be invalid and a
determination by the Mayor that any related issues should be picked
up outside of the meeting.

The motion was seconded by Councillor
Roberts.  It was noted that the Chief
Executive’s decision not to accept the motion had been
discussed both at the start of meeting under Urgent Business and
towards the end of the meeting under Notices of Motion.

Councillor Rice asked the Mayor whether the Council
could hold a minute’s silence in recognition of the terrible
situation faced by the residents of Gaza.  The Mayor welcomed the suggestion and advised that
the Council would first deal with the motion put forward by the
Leader.

Councillor Akberali welcomed the proposal to amend
the minutes of the meeting of Council on 25 September 2025 to
reflect his requests at the meeting for his motion to be considered
by the Council, arguing that he had been stifled at the meeting and
that preventing consideration of his motion was
undemocratic.

The Mayor referred the Council to the motion put
forward by the Leader of the Council which was agreed nem con.

RESOLVED

That the minutes of the meeting of Council held on
25 September 2025 be amended as follows:

Item 5. Urgent Business to read:

“The Mayor advised that there were no items of
Urgent Business to consider.  Councillor
Akberali requested an opportunity to speak in regard to his Notice
of Motion on Gaza under this item.  The
Mayor advised that the request was not a matter of Urgent Business
and could not be accepted.”

Item 15 Notices of Motion to read:

“The Mayor reported that no valid notices of
motion had been received.  Councillor
Akberali requested an opportunity to speak as a point of order,
advising that the Mayor’s statement was
misleading.  The Chief Executive,
Richard Carr, explained that he was required under the Constitution
to determine whether or not a motion was valid.  In the case of Councillor Akberali’s Notice
of Motion, he had judged that the motion was not valid for the
reasons previously explained to Councillor Akberali in
correspondence.  The Mayor’s
statement was therefore accurate.

Councillor Akberali asked what course of action he
could take if the Motion was not accepted, highlighting
consequences of ignoring people’s concerns and equating it to
mistakes in the past.  The Mayor advised
Councillor Akberali to raise the matter outside of the
meeting.”

Following the decision, the Council held a
minute’s silence in recognition of the terrible situation
faced by the residents of Gaza.
topline: The Council has decided to amend the minutes of a meeting to reflect the discussion around a motion on Gaza that was deemed invalid, sparking controversy among councillors.

The Calendar of Meetings for 2026/27 was before the Council for

Calendar had been amended following confirmation of the
Government’s Local Government Reorganisation proposals which
would see the abolition of the current two tier system on 31 March
2027.  Accordingly, no Council Committee
dates had been set beyond 31 March 2027, with the final meeting of
Woking Borough Council being Full Council scheduled for Thursday,
18 March 2027.
Group Leaders and Deputy Group Leaders, along with the Chairs
and Vice-Chairs of the Scrutiny Committees, had been consulted on
the proposed Calendar.
The Leader of the Council, Councillor Barker, advised that, as
in previous years, additional meetings of the
Council and Committees could be arranged if necessary.  It was noted that the Calendar would result in a
large gap between the meeting of Council in September 2026 and
December 2026.  In view of this, the
Leader proposed that the meeting of Council scheduled for 24
September 2026 should be moved to 15 October 2026.  The meeting of the Executive which was proposed in
the report for 15 October 2026 would be moved to 8 October 2026,
providing a better spread of Council meetings.  Councillor Roberts seconded the
proposal.
A
typographical error was highlighted; the report made reference to a
meeting of the Chair’s Forum being held in December 2027
which would be corrected to read December 2026.

Resolved

That the Calendar of Meetings 2026/27 be approved as
set out in Appendix 1 to the report, subject to:

·               
the date of the last Chairs’ Forum being
amended to 9 December 2026;

·               
the meeting of Council proposed for 24 September
2026 be moved to 15 October 2026; and

·               
the meeting of the Executive proposed for 15 October
2026 be moved to 8 October 2026.

content:
The Council received a report on the results of the Stage 1
consultation on the Community Governance Review (CGR) for the
Pyrford area, which had been requested earlier in the year by the
Pyrford Neighbourhood Forum. 
The majority of respondents had supported the
proposals, with 68% having been in favour.  The report set out a series
of recommendations which would form the basis of a second round of
public and stakeholder consultations to be undertaken in January
and February 2026.
The proposal was based on the assumption of a single electoral
area which would be represented by ten parish councillors who would
be elected to that area.  It was hoped
that the proposals would address some of the concerns raised by
respondents, including the loss of democratic representation and
the lack of local representation under the local government
reorganisation.
Members were advised that it was expected that, following the
conclusion of the Review, the earliest any Reorganisation Order
would come into effect would be March 2027, with elections held in
May 2027.  The proposals would have cost
implications which the Council would need to address in due
course.
The proposals were introduced by the
Leader of the Council and Portfolio Holder for democratic and civic
functions, Councillor Barker.  It had
been intended to start the consultation on New Year’s
Day.  However, it was moved by the
Leader and seconded by Councillor Lyons that the start date should
be moved to 6 January 2026.  The
consultation would conclude at the end of February
2026.  The amendment was agreed nem
con.
Before asking the Members to agree the proposals, a
typographical error in the recommendations was highlighted;
reference to ‘January’ would be removed from the final
recommendation (iii).

Resolved

That  (i)      the responses from the Stage 1
consultation process which took place from 1 October to 30 November
2025, as set out in Appendices 1 and 2, be carefully
considered;

         
(ii)     the draft
recommendations for the Community Governance Review as set out in
Appendix 3 be approved;

         
(iii)    the draft recommendations
be subject to a period of consultation from 6 January – 28
February 2026; and

         
(iv)    authority be delegated to
the Director of Legal and Democratic Services in consultation with
the Community Governance Review Working Group to agree the
consultation documents and to make any minor amendments to all of
the documents as may be required prior to the start of the
consultation.
topline: The Council has decided to approve draft recommendations for the Community Governance Review in the Pyrford area, with a majority of respondents in favor of the proposals.

purpose:
To receive an update on Local Government
Reorganisation.
content:
Councillor Lyons introduced the report of the Executive which
set out the next steps in the process towards
setting up the new shadow local authority.  The first of these was the structural change order
which would set out various arrangements for the period up to
Investing Day on 1 April 2027 when West Surrey would go
live.  The Chief Executive of Surrey
County Council, Terrence Herbert, would act as the Senior
Responsible Officer to oversee the transition across the current
local authority of Surrey.
One of the key aspects of the structural change order was the
creation of two joint committees comprising of elected members from
Surrey County Council and each of the district and borough
councils. These Committees would initially be established on a
voluntary basis initially before being formalised in March 2026,
and would have strong executive functions over high level decisions
of the shadow unitary authorities, including budget setting.
 Any costs associated with the changes
would be borne by each of the current local authorities; Woking
Borough Council's contribution had been calculated to be
£642,000.  In order to prepare for
expected and unexpected costs, the Council had set aside a budget
of £1m in the 2026 -27 budget.
The Members of the Council noted the information set out in the
report.  The importance of keeping
Councillors informed of the activities of the Joint Committee and
the intention to webcast the meetings of the Committee were
welcomed.  It was hoped that as many
decisions as possible would be taken in public and that only those
decisions which contained exempt information as defined by
legislation would be held in private.
The Mayor thanked the Portfolio Holder and referred the Members
to the recommendations before them.

Resolved

That (i)   the LGR updates as set out in the Executive
report dated 4 December 2025 be noted;

       
(ii)  the approval by the Executive on 4
December 2025 of the establishment of the Joint Committees and the
Terms of Reference be noted; and

       
(iii)  the
appointment of Councillor Barker and Councillor Lyons as Woking
Borough Council’s representative and substitute to the West
Surrey Voluntary Joint Committee followed by the statutory West
Surrey Joint Committee be approved.
topline: The Council has decided to establish new shadow local authority in West Surrey with joint committees having executive functions.

content:
The Council had before it a report which proposed that a
Community Governance Review (CGR) of the whole of the Woking
Borough Council area (with the exception of the Pyrford
Neighbourhood area) should be undertaken.  The Review would be subject to approval of the
required budget as part of the 2026/27 budget setting process in
February 2026.  In the event the budget
was approved, a further report would be presented to Council
setting out the proposed terms of reference and
timetable.
The Leader explained her concern that, under the unitary
arrangements, the residents would have much reduced local
representation, with the number of elected representatives reducing
from 37 to 14.  Other areas in the new West Surrey unitary had existing parishes
or were looking to create parishes.  The
Parish Councils could be made responsible for some of the
responsibilities of the new unitary authority.
The costs of a Borough-wide review would be significant and the
Leader would ensure that the work would be undertaken in the most
cost-effective way, potentially using online communications in
place of sending letters to every household.  It was essential, however, that the Council sought
the views of residents to ensure suitable local representation was
provided.
Councillors debated the proposals and added concern was
expressed over the potential loss of the ceremonial function of the
Council, in particular the role of the Mayor.  The matter was highlighted in the hope that it
would not get lost in the overall reorganisation of the local
authorities.  Councillor Barker
responded to the concerns raised, noting that the loss of the role
of the Mayor had been raised by a number of people.

Resolved

That a Borough-wide Community Governance Review be
approved (excluding the Pyrford Neighbourhood Area) subject to
approval by Full Council in February 2026 of the necessary budget
required for the Community Governance Review.
topline: The Council has decided to undertake a Borough-wide Community Governance Review, excluding the Pyrford Neighbourhood Area.

purpose:
To seek approval for the adoption of the List
of Locally Listed Heritage Assets ‘The Local
List’.
content:
The Council considered the recommendations in respect of the
Local List of Heritage Assets.  The
report considered by the Executive provided an overview of the
outcome of the draft Local List consultation.  The consultation on the draft Local List had
concluded, with all comments summarised and responded
to.  Modifications had been made to the
Local List document in light of the responses received.
It
was now proposed that the Local List should be approved for
adoption and become a ‘living’ document which would
form a material consideration in planning decisions affecting
non-designated heritage assets.  The
Portfolio Holder, Councillor Morales, advised that inclusion on the
list did not prevent development but required planning officers to
consider historical context.
Some properties had been removed from the list following
significant changes to the assets, such as the former White Hart
pub in Old Woking which had been converted into flats and had lost
its historical character.  Many new
assets had, however, been added to the list, including the
Colquhoun Chapel in Brookwood Cemetery, a Victorian sewer pipe in
Pyrford and the Martians landing place on Horsell Common,
associated with H.G. Wells’ famous novel.  It was further noted that 141 Maybury Road, the former residence of HG Wells, had been
added to the list after efforts by the HG Wells Society to secure
protection for the property.
The report was welcomed by the Council and it was suggested that
the Council should explore how some of the history could be shared
with residents.  A number of points were
raised by Members including the absence from the list of the cart
barn associated with a grade two listed
building and the consideration that not all owners welcomed the
inclusion of their property on the list.  It was also noted that the
Pyrford Forum was yet to receive a response from Officers in
respect of a list of 30 assets the Forum had put forward for
inclusion on the list.
The Portfolio Holder responded to the points raised.  It was noted that the cart barn formed part of the
listed building which afforded greater protection than a locally
listed building.  The barn could be
reviewed, however, for inclusion on the next edition of the
list.  It was recognised that not
everyone would want to see their property included on the list,
though it was noted that, for those wishing to change their
property, the listing did not require a separate listed building
consent.
The suggestion that the Council could promote the history of the
Borough to residents was welcomed, though with so many priorities
faced by the Council it was not known whether resources would be
available for such a piece of work.  The
Portfolio Holder encouraged the Councillors to consider how they
could promote the history within their wards to local residents
through social media.

Resolved

That (i)   the Draft
Local List and accompanying mapping be adopted as a
‘living’ document; and

       
(ii)  the contents of the Officer
Response Table (Appendix 1 to the report) to the consultation and
Draft Local List (Appendix 2 to the report) be
considered.

Community and stakeholder consultation,
Cllr Morales, Portfolio Holder.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the Local List of Heritage Assets as a 'living' document, affecting planning decisions for non-designated heritage assets.

purpose:
To seek approval of the procurement strategy
for a Main Contractor for the Lakeview Estate Refurbishment Scheme
and approval for the procurement to progress via a compliant
Framework.
content:
To seek approval of the procurement strategy
for a Main Contractor for the Lakeview Estate Refurbishment Scheme
and approval for the procurement to progress via a compliant
Framework.


The Executive
Resolved

That  (i)    approval be
granted to commence procurement of a contractor to deliver the
Lakeview Estate Refurbishment Scheme;

         
(ii)   procurement will be
undertaken through the London Construction Programme Housing Major
Works framework (LCP MW24-H Framework (Lot 2.3)) by way of a
mini-competition;

         
(iii)  the Head of Housing Assets, in
consultation with the Strategic Director – Communities, be
authorised to progress the procurement and return to Executive for
approval of the contract award; and

         
(iv)  leaseholders will not be recharged
for the element of the proposed works which consists of
cladding/external wall system replacement, but will be recharged
for other Qualifying Works.

Reason: To fulfil the Council’s statutory
responsibilities for resident safety and building compliance and
ensure the buildings remain habitable through replacement of
temporary fire safety measures with permanent solutions, and to
address end-of-life components such as roofs, windows, and doors
alongside external wall systems.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the procurement strategy for a Main Contractor for the Lakeview Estate Refurbishment Scheme.

content:
To consider additional information on the
disposal of vacant housing land to ThamesWey for the Yellow phase
of the regeneration project along with an update on the disposal of
remaining development parcels and confirm agreement to proceed with
both transfers.


The Executive Resolved

That  (i)    in response to the HRA Forensic Review
reported to Council on 25 September 2025, the Council transfers the
vacant Housing land for Yellow phase of the Sheerwater regeneration
project to ThamesWey Developments Limited for the revised sum of
£3,029,811 (comprising £2,504,511 debt value, plus the
reimbursement of £525,300 of costs incurred by the HRA in
compensating tenants);

         
(ii)   it be confirmed that the
remaining three development land parcels should be sold freehold to
the selected bidder as previously approved by the Executive on the
14 November 2024 in the light of the additional information
included within the
Exempt Part 2 Report; and

         
(iii)  authority be delegated to the
Strategic Director - Communities, in consultation with the
Portfolio Holder for Housing and the Director of Legal and
Democratic Services, to take all necessary steps to effect the
recommendations in (i) and (ii), including entering into any
necessary legal documents.

Reason: To support the continued delivery of the
Council’s vision for the Sheerwater regeneration, but on a
smaller scale and with less reliance on public funds.

Cllrs Johnson and Roberts, Portfolio
Holders.
topline: The Executive has decided to transfer vacant housing land and sell remaining development parcels for the Sheerwater regeneration project.

Cllrs Johnson and Roberts, Portfolio
Holders.
